title: Proteomic analysis of gemcitabine-resistant (GemR) versus paired control human pancreatic cancer cells (PCCs)
projectDescription: In search of potential markers of treatment response, comparative LC-MS/MS-based proteomic analysis of GemR and paired control PCCs was performed. It includes four different PCC lines including three primary - PCC-1 (c1), PCC-2 (c2), PCC-7 (c3) and Mia PaCa-2 (c4). Cells were maintained in DMEM supplemented with 10% FBS, with or without gemcitabine (50-150 nM) for upto 40 passages. Cell lysates in triplicate from GemR and paired control cells collected at six different passages (p10, p20, p25, p30, p35, and p40) during treatment period were analyzed using LC-MS/MS
sampleProcessingProtocol: Cells seeded in 6-well plates at a density of 100 000 cells per well in 2 mL medium were harvested upon reaching at least 50% confluence using RIPA lysis buffer (160 µL/well) supplemented with protease and phosphatase Inhibitors. 10 µg protein from each lysate was precipitated on amine beads and dissolved in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate, reduced, alkylated, and digested with trypsin at 37°C overnight. Digested peptides were acidified and desalted on EVOTIPs using a standard protocol from EVOSEP. LC-MS/MS was carried out using an EVOSEP one LC system (EVOSEP Biosystems, Odense, Denmark) coupled to a timsTOF Pro2 mass spectrometer, using a CaptiveSpray nanoelectrospray ion source (Bruker Corporation, Germany). 200 ng digested peptides were loaded onto a capillary C18 column (15 cm length, 150 μm inner diameter, 1.5 μm particle size; EVOSEP). Peptides were separated at 40C using the standard 30 sample/day method from EVOSEP. The timsTOF Pro2 mass spectrometer was operated in DIA-PASEF mode. Mass spectra were recorded between m/z 100 and 1700. Ion mobility resolution was set to 0.85-1.30 V s/cm over a ramp time of 100 ms. MS/MS mass range was limited to m/z 475-1000 and ion mobility resolution to 0.85-1.27 V s/cm to exclude singly charged ions. The estimated cycle time was 0.95 s with 8 cycles using DIA windows of 25 Da. Collisional energy was ramped from 20eV at 0.60 V s/cm to 59eV at 1.60 V s/cm.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw data files from LC-MS/MS analysis were submitted to DIA-NN software version 1.8.1 for protein identification and label-free quantification using the library-free function. The UniProt human database (European Bioinformatics Institute, EMBL-EBI, UK) was used to generate a library in silico from a human FASTA file. Carbamidomethyl (C) was set as a fixed modification. Trypsin without proline restriction enzyme option was used, with one allowed miscleavage, and peptide length range was set to 7-30 amino acids. The mass accuracy was set to 15 ppm and the precursor false discovery rate (FDR) allowed was 0.01 (1%). MS/MS data quality evaluation and initial statistical analysis were done using Perseus software version 2.0.11.0 (Max-Planck Institute of Biochemistry, Martinsried, Germany).
